title: Hubble / Policy Verdicts (Namespace)

list.name: role
list.label: namespace is the
list.description: Which side of the verdict the namespace filter applies to: the destination (what came INTO the namespace and what the policy did — the default) or the source (what the namespace's workloads tried to reach). Demo 29 Part 8: an egress drop that leaves the namespace is on the source side only.

panels.title: 1 · Policy verdicts — what the policy decided (hubble_policy_verdicts_total)
Audited (policy evaluated, not enforced) — in range
Forwarded by an allow rule — in range
Still audited (last 5 min): source → destination pairs
panels.description: A source → destination pair that produced audit verdicts in the last 5 minutes has an endpoint in PolicyAuditMode: policy is evaluated and reported, nothing is blocked yet. Green 'none' means every endpoint in view is enforcing (or nothing is selected by a policy at all — the audit and dropped counters say which). Pairs, not workloads, so the count reads the same whether the namespace is the destination or the source. The query is INSTANT: a stat over a range series reduces lastNotNull and would show the last value from the audit window long after audit was switched off — measured on the first capture.

panels.title: Policy verdicts per second, by action
panels.description: hubble_policy_verdicts_total — Hubble's `policy` dynamic metric (the chart README). An audit line rising while forwarded/dropped stay flat is the observe-first phase; dropped appearing after audit vanishes is enforcement.

panels.title: Verdicts per second, by source → destination and action
Who talked to whom, and what the policy did — totals in range

targets.expr: sum(increase(hubble_policy_verdicts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", ${role}=~"$namespace"}[$__range])) by (cluster, source, destination, direction, action, match)

panels.description: match = none means no allow rule matched (the default-deny decided: audit while observing, dropped when enforcing); l3-l4 / l3-only / l4-only / l7 name the rule kind that allowed the flow.

panels.title: POLICY_DENIED drops per second (hubble_drop_total)
panels.description: Cilium's drop metric beside the verdict metric: the same enforcement seen by the datapath (reason POLICY_DENIED), per source → destination. The same drops the Network Overview and the Hubble Metrics 'Network Policy' row show — here beside the audit line, so the before/after of enforcement is one picture.

panels.title: 2 · Flows — everything Hubble saw, every verdict
Flows in range
panels.description: Flow events Hubble processed for the namespace (as ${role}) in the time range, any verdict. Hubble counts on every node that saw the flow, so a flow that crosses two nodes is counted on both: this number is not comparable to the section 1 verdict tiles (hubble_policy_verdicts_total, counted at the enforcement point).

panels.title: Forwarded in range
panels.description: Flows with verdict FORWARDED.

panels.title: Dropped in range
panels.description: Flows with verdict DROPPED — any reason, policy or not (section 3 says which).

panels.title: Peers seen
panels.description: Distinct source → destination pairs among the namespace's flows in range.

panels.title: Flows per second, by verdict
panels.description: Every flow Hubble processed for the namespace (as ${role}), by verdict — FORWARDED, DROPPED, AUDIT, REDIRECTED, ERROR. The verdict panels above count POLICY decisions only; this is the whole traffic they sit in. From Cilium's Hubble / Network Overview (Namespace) dashboard, scoped by the same namespace filter as the rest of this page. Counted on every node that saw the flow (a flow crossing two nodes counts twice).

panels.description: The busiest sources among the namespace's flows (as ${role}), now.

panels.title: Top 10 destinations (flows per second)
panels.description: The busiest destinations among the namespace's flows (as ${role}), now.

Drops in range
panels.description: Packets dropped for the namespace (as ${role}), every reason.

panels.title: Policy drops in range
panels.description: Of those, reason POLICY_DENIED — the verdicts of section 1, seen by the datapath.

panels.title: Other reasons in range
panels.description: Drops that are NOT a policy verdict: unroutable, no service backend, conntrack, … — the chart names them.

panels.title: Reasons seen
panels.description: How many distinct drop reasons occurred in range.

panels.title: Drops per second, by reason and protocol
panels.description: All of Cilium's drop reasons for the namespace (as ${role}), not only POLICY_DENIED: a drop that is not a policy verdict (an unroutable address, a missing service backend, a conntrack miss) shows here and nowhere in the verdict panels. From Cilium's Hubble Metrics 'Network Policy' row and the Network Overview drops, in one panel.

panels.title: Top 10 sources with dropped packets
panels.description: Who is being dropped the most (any reason), now. The reason is on the timeseries to the left.

panels.title: Top 10 destinations with dropped packets
panels.description: Whose traffic is being dropped on the way in (any reason), now. The reason is on the timeseries to the left.

panels.title: 4 · Connection health — attempts that never completed
SYNs sent in range
panels.description: TCP connection attempts by the namespace's sources (as ${role}).

panels.title: Missing SYN-ACKs in range
panels.description: SYNs that got no SYN-ACK back — attempts that never completed. Green at zero. Matched by identity and namespace; with `namespace is the destination` it can under-count (see the chart).

targets.expr: clamp_min(sum(sum by (source, source_namespace) (increase(hubble_tcp_flags_total{cluster=~"$cluster", ${role}=~"$namespace", flag="SYN"}[$__range]))) - sum(sum by (destination, destination_namespace) (increase(hubble_tcp_flags_total{cluster=~"$cluster", flag="SYN-ACK"}[$__range])) and on (destination, destination_namespace) label_replace(label_replace(sum by (source, source_namespace) (increase(hubble_tcp_flags_total{cluster=~"$cluster", ${role}=~"$namespace", flag="SYN"}[$__range])), "destination", "$1", "source", "(.*)"), "destination_namespace", "$1", "source_namespace", "(.*)")), 0)

panels.title: Echo requests in range
panels.description: ICMP echo requests (pings) from the namespace.

panels.title: Missing echo replies in range
panels.description: Pings that got no reply. Green at zero. Matched by identity and namespace; with `namespace is the destination` it can under-count (see the chart).

targets.expr: clamp_min(sum(sum by (source, source_namespace) (increase(hubble_icmp_total{cluster=~"$cluster", ${role}=~"$namespace", type="EchoRequest"}[$__range]))) - sum(sum by (destination, destination_namespace) (increase(hubble_icmp_total{cluster=~"$cluster", type="EchoReply"}[$__range])) and on (destination, destination_namespace) label_replace(label_replace(sum by (source, source_namespace) (increase(hubble_icmp_total{cluster=~"$cluster", ${role}=~"$namespace", type="EchoRequest"}[$__range])), "destination", "$1", "source", "(.*)"), "destination_namespace", "$1", "source_namespace", "(.*)")), 0)

panels.title: TCP: SYNs sent, SYN-ACKs received, and the missing ones
panels.description: SYNs the namespace's sources sent (as ${role}) minus the SYN-ACKs that came back to them: a connection attempt that never completes — a silent drop somewhere, a backend that is not listening, a policy on the far side. Cilium's own query from the Network Overview dashboard; the reply direction is matched by swapping source and destination. Replies are matched by workload identity AND namespace (source and destination are Cilium identities — app, workload-name, reserved-identity — not pod names). With `namespace is the destination`, the senders are the namespace's CLIENTS, and replies those clients got from OTHER servers count too, so 'missing' can under-count there; the source side is the exact reading.

targets.expr: sum(sum by (destination, destination_namespace) (rate(hubble_tcp_flags_total{cluster=~"$cluster", flag="SYN-ACK"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (destination, destination_namespace) label_replace(label_replace(sum by (source, source_namespace) (rate(hubble_tcp_flags_total{cluster=~"$cluster", ${role}=~"$namespace", flag="SYN"}[$__rate_interval])), "destination", "$1", "source", "(.*)"), "destination_namespace", "$1", "source_namespace", "(.*)"))

(sum by (source, source_namespace) (rate(hubble_tcp_flags_total{cluster=~"$cluster", ${role}=~"$namespace", flag="SYN"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum by (source, source_namespace) (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (destination, destination_namespace) (rate(hubble_tcp_flags_total{cluster=~"$cluster", flag="SYN-ACK"}[$__rate_interval])), "source", "$1", "destination", "(.*)"), "source_namespace", "$1", "destination_namespace", "(.*)"))) > 0

panels.title: ICMP: echo requests, replies, and the missing ones
panels.description: Echo requests from the namespace (as ${role}) that got no reply. Same shape as the SYN-ACK panel, for pings. Replies are matched by workload identity AND namespace (source and destination are Cilium identities — app, workload-name, reserved-identity — not pod names). With `namespace is the destination`, the senders are the namespace's CLIENTS, and replies those clients got from OTHER servers count too, so 'missing' can under-count there; the source side is the exact reading.

targets.expr: sum(sum by (destination, destination_namespace) (rate(hubble_icmp_total{cluster=~"$cluster", type="EchoReply"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (destination, destination_namespace) label_replace(label_replace(sum by (source, source_namespace) (rate(hubble_icmp_total{cluster=~"$cluster", ${role}=~"$namespace", type="EchoRequest"}[$__rate_interval])), "destination", "$1", "source", "(.*)"), "destination_namespace", "$1", "source_namespace", "(.*)"))

(sum by (source, source_namespace) (rate(hubble_icmp_total{cluster=~"$cluster", ${role}=~"$namespace", type="EchoRequest"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum by (source, source_namespace) (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (destination, destination_namespace) (rate(hubble_icmp_total{cluster=~"$cluster", type="EchoReply"}[$__rate_interval])), "source", "$1", "destination", "(.*)"), "source_namespace", "$1", "destination_namespace", "(.*)"))) > 0

panels.title: Queries in range
panels.description: DNS lookups the namespace's workloads sent.

panels.title: Answered in range
panels.description: Answers that came back to them, any rcode.

panels.title: Missing answers in range
panels.description: Lookups with no answer back. Green at zero.

panels.title: Errors in range
panels.description: Answers that were not 'No Error' (NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, REFUSED). Green at zero.

panels.title: DNS queries per second, by record type
panels.description: Lookups the namespace's workloads sent, by qtype. This row does not follow the 'namespace is the' switch: a lookup's destination is always the resolver (kube-system, or openshift-dns), so the namespace here is the source of the query and the destination of the answer. From Cilium's Hubble / DNS Overview (Namespace) dashboard.

panels.title: DNS errors, by answer code
panels.description: Answers to the namespace that were not 'No Error': NXDOMAIN (a name that does not exist — a typo, a Service in the wrong namespace), SERVFAIL, REFUSED (a toFQDNs policy's DNS proxy refusing a name outside the rules).

panels.title: DNS: queries, answers, and the missing ones
panels.description: Lookups that got no answer back to the asking pod — the resolver unreachable, or the answer dropped on the way back (a policy that allows 53 out but not the reply is the classic).

panels.title: Top 10 names asked (queries per minute)
panels.description: What the namespace resolves most, now — the names a toFQDNs rule would have to allow.

Requests in range
panels.description: HTTP requests to the namespace's workloads (as ${role}), from Hubble's httpV2 metric as the SERVER reported them (the client's copy would double-count). Needs an L7 policy or visibility annotation on the port — without one Cilium's proxy does not see HTTP.

panels.title: 5xx in range
panels.description: Responses with a 5xx status. Green at zero.

panels.title: p50 latency
panels.description: Median request duration over the range.

panels.title: p99 latency
panels.description: 99th-percentile request duration over the range.

panels.title: Requests per second, by status
panels.description: Requests per second by HTTP status, server-reported.

panels.title: Request duration p50 / p99, with trace exemplars
panels.description: Latency percentiles from the histogram. The dots are exemplars: a request whose trace id Cilium's proxy read from the traceparent header — click one to open the trace in Tempo (the Prometheus datasource must map exemplar trace ids to a Tempo datasource; kube-prometheus-stack: exemplarTraceIdDestinations).

panels.title: Top 10 source → destination workloads (requests per second)
panels.description: Who calls whom over HTTP, now.

panels.title: Top 10 methods and status (requests per second)
panels.description: Method × status, now: a 4xx or 5xx column stands out here.

description: Policy verdicts from Hubble's `policy` dynamic metric (hubble_policy_verdicts_total): audit (observe first), forwarded (an allow rule matched), dropped (enforced), per namespace, with the drop metric beside them — and, since 0.3.0, the namespace's whole traffic around those verdicts: flows by verdict, drops of every reason, missing SYN-ACKs and echo replies, DNS queries, errors and missing answers (the panels of Cilium's Hubble Network Overview and DNS Overview namespace dashboards, on this page's namespace filter). Source: https://github.com/ephico2real2/hubble-policy-verdicts
